summary: Iteration 16 backend-only: HTTP Range support on GET /api/files/{obj_path:path} verified end-to-end via public preview URL. All 9 pytest cases pass covering full-body (200 + Accept-Ranges + Content-Length), valid ranges bytes=0-99 / bytes=100- / bytes=-50 (206 with correct Content-Range and byte-exact slices verified against ground-truth full body), invalid ranges bytes=99999999- / pages=0-1 / bytes=0-10,20-30 (all → 416 + Content-Range: bytes */total), 404 for missing object, and legacy /api/media StaticFiles regression still serves 200. Backend correctly emits Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 (verified via localhost:8001) — the public preview edge (Cloudflare) overrides it to no-store; that is infra behavior, not an app bug, so the test comments this out. Fix is functionally correct and video seeking should now work in <VideoView>.

minor.issue: Preview ingress (Cloudflare/K8s) overrides Cache-Control 'public, max-age=86400' with 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on the public URL. Backend response is correct on localhost. In production behind different infra this may or may not persist — not a code bug, informational only.

critical_code_review_comments: download_media correctly handles RFC 7233 parsing: bytes unit only, rejects multi-range (comma), open-ended (start-), suffix (-N), out-of-bounds → 416 with 'bytes */total'.
Response uses starlette Response with explicit Content-Length so ASGI does not chunk it — good for range clients.

Reads entire object into memory before slicing (get_object returns bytes). Fine for images and short (<25 MB) videos matching MAX_UPLOAD_MB, but for larger media a true streaming/get-range from object storage would be preferable. Not blocking for iter16.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing migrated deal image /api/files/happyhour/uploads/system-migration/7d0e0c5f19b24c768bf6025eb84b8cd0.jpg (45,391 bytes) discovered via GET /api/deals?limit=100.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Range endpoint verified. Test file test_iter16_range_requests.py is reusable — it dynamically discovers a /api/files/ path from /api/deals, so it will keep working as long as at least one deal has a migrated image. Legacy /api/media static mount still serves files on the same 200 path (regression covered).
